title: ARC-AGI-2 smoke: hypothesis-first pass on 5 fresh training tasks
goal: Solve at least one of the five sealed ARC-AGI-2 training tasks in assets/gc-441/task_ids.txt, but in a hypothesis-first discipline: for each task, write the candidate rule in plain language before producing any grid, mechanically re-derive every train output from that rule, and only then apply it to the test input. If the re-derivation misses even one train pair the hypothesis must be revised and re-verified, not patched by eye. Ship runs/gc-441/predictions.json, grade it with assets/gc-441/grade.py, and if the verdict is short of threshold, pick the nearest-miss task, revise its rule, and grade again inside the one-day horizon.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-441/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 5 task ids, one per line; all from the public training split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-441/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-441/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-441/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-441/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-441/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
